title: streaming: add robust lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, and reconnect/resume
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Users reported intermittent partial-streams and duplicate events when clients cancel, disconnect mid-stream, or reconnect. This caused state inconsistencies in the server-side stream runtime (stale KV cache pointers, lingering in-flight tasks, and double-emits when clients resumed). This PR adds explicit lifecycle controls across the streaming stack to make client cancel, disconnect, and reconnect/resume behavior deterministic and compatible with our OpenAI-compat streaming adapter.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a CancelToken propagated from the transport (HTTP/WS) into the runtime so server work can be preempted on client cancel.
- Adds a graceful disconnect handler: on TCP/WS disconnect, we mark the stream as disconnected (retain limited resume state for X seconds), cancel non-committed in-progress work, and flush buffered events with a final tombstone event where appropriate.
- Implements reconnect/resume semantics: client-provided resume_token can reattach to retained stream state; server validates token and replays buffered events up to a soft limit to catch the client up without re-running heavy model work.
- Tightens server-side timeouts: per-stream idle timeout and per-request compute timeout with clear metrics and logs for timeout reason.
- Ensures OpenAI compatibility: streaming_adapter now emits the same event shapes and error semantics expected by the OpenAI-compatible SDKs (stream close events, error events, final completion).
- Adds end-to-end tests for cancel, disconnect, resume, and timeout cases across HTTP streaming and WebSocket transports.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Resume is best-effort: we retain a bounded buffer (configurable, default 50 events / 30s) to avoid high memory usage for long-running streams. If buffer is expired or missing, clients will receive a non-recoverable resume error and must restart the request.
- CancelToken cancellation is cooperative: long-running kernels are checked at pre-agreed safe points to avoid inconsistent GPU state. Where kernel-level preemption isn't available, we ensure proper KV cache cleanup before acknowledging cancellation.
- We intentionally emit a tombstone final event on disconnects that closed without completion so clients can deterministically clean up UI state.

Backwards compatibility:
- Default behavior is compatible with existing clients. Resume requires an explicit resume_token (opt-in). The OpenAI compatibility layer will continue to accept older streaming shapes until EOL, but new informative close/error events are added to improve robustness.

Testing and verification:
- Added unit tests for CancelToken propagation and timeout cancellation.
- Added integration tests that simulate flaky networks: abrupt WS close, TCP reconnect, HTTP client abort.
- Canary runs in perf lab showed no measurable tail-latency regression for small streams; large-stream memory bounded as expected.

Checklist (completed):
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-8742)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] SDK compatibility tested (python/js)
- [x] Docs added (docs/streaming-lifecycle.md)
- [x] Metrics & tracing added for cancel/disconnect/timeouts

Migration: No DB or schema migrations. Operators can tune resume buffer window with new flags: streaming.resume_buffer_size and streaming.resume_retention_seconds.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on connection_manager cancellation semantics and the OpenAI adapter mapping for error/tombstone events. I called out spots where I added TODOs for future kernel-level preemption work.

Aisha Patel: We added a cooperative checkpointing point before writes. If kernel preemption isn't available, we perform cache cleanup in the finally path and emit a tombstone so downstream knows to invalidate state.

merge_summary: Squash merged by Jun Park after approvals. No DB migrations. Rollout: gradual on hosted API with a 48h canary flag, operators can tune resume buffer via streaming.resume_buffer_size and streaming.resume_retention_seconds.
release_notes:
- streaming: add lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, and reconnect/resume.
 - OpenAI-compat: improved error/close events and optional resume_token support.
 - Config: streaming.resume_buffer_size, streaming.resume_retention_seconds.
notes_to_ops: Default resume retention is conservative (30s/50 events). Recommend enabling canary in low-traffic region first. Monitor metrics: streaming.cancel_count, streaming.disconnect_count, streaming.resume_replay_count, streaming.timeout_terminations.
impact_assessment: Memory: bounded by resume buffer config. Latency: negligible change for short streams, small additional latency when replaying buffer on resume (observed < 20ms per small event). No breaking changes for existing clients by default.
